text: Writing clean code is essential for anyone who wants to develop software efficiently. The most important goal is to make your code readable, both for yourself and for others. One key practice is following naming conventions: use clear and descriptive names for variables, functions, and classes, so their purpose is obvious at a glance. Additionally, each function should do one specific thing and do it well. This makes your code modular and easier to test. By keeping functions small and focused, you improve maintainability, meaning that future changes or bug fixes will be much simpler and less risky to implement.
